title: Long a Baby’s Brand, Carter’s Grows Into Kids
summary: Carter's, a legacy baby and kids brand, is expanding its size range to include sizes 10 to 14, marking a significant push into the kids' market. This move is part of a larger strategy to boost volume by $1 billion over five years, driven partly by e-commerce, and includes reconfiguring retail stores and enhancing product categories. The new collection, launching in June, aims to offer playful and trendy styles while empowering children's individuality.

title: CVS Says It’s Still ‘Moving Forward’ With $68 Billion Aetna Deal
summary: CVS Health Corp. is progressing with the regulatory review of its $68 billion acquisition of Aetna Inc. and has suspended its share buyback program pending approval. CEO Larry Merlo anticipates a close in the second half of the year, with plans to integrate Aetna's 22 million customers with CVS's 10,000 stores to create healthcare hubs. The deal is currently under review by the Justice Department alongside a similar megamerger between Express Scripts and Cigna.

title: Best Buy details CEO Hubert Joly's raise, median worker pay
summary: Best Buy's Chairman and CEO, Hubert Joly, received over $16.7 million in compensation, a 19 percent increase primarily due to a boost in non-equity incentive plan compensation. This disclosure details the executive's significant pay package.

title: SoundHound Secures $100M To Amp Voice AI Platform, New Alliances.
summary: Sound-recognition company SoundHound has secured $100 million in new funding, bringing its total funding to $215 million. The company plans to use the funds to drive the adoption and distribution of its Houndify voice AI platform across various verticals and accelerate global expansion. This funding also forges alliances with leading companies like Tencent Holdings and Daimler AG, providing access to over 2 billion consumers globally.

title: Starbucks' Howard Schultz at Morehouse: 'We live in an age of anger, rage, racial tension'
summary: Starbucks executives Howard Schultz and Rosalind Gates Brewer held a town hall meeting at Morehouse College, where Schultz addressed the prevalent "anger, rage, racial tension" in society. The meeting followed Starbucks' announcement to close all its stores on May 29 for racial-bias education. Related articles highlight Brewer's potential as the next Starbucks CEO and the company's recent activities.

title: Pro gamer from Wayne competing for Knicks in NBA 2K League
summary: Adam Kudeimati, a 19-year-old from Wayne, New Jersey, was drafted by Knicks Gaming for the inaugural NBA 2K League, fulfilling his dream of playing professionally for his favorite team. Kudeimati, known as "iamadamthe1st," was one of 102 gamers selected from a pool of 72,000 players and is earning a $32,000 salary with potential for significant prize money, medical benefits, and free food and lodging in Jersey City. Beyond gaming, Kudeimati is an online Penn State student with a passion for acting, photography, and videography, managing a YouTube channel with over 311,000 subscribers.

title: Best Buy rebrands around blue-shirts, unveils new logo (video)
summary: Best Buy is undergoing a rebranding effort that will highlight the expertise of its store employees, known for their blue-shirt uniforms. The retailer plans to launch new TV advertisements this week featuring its staff and will also introduce a new logo. This move aims to emphasize the in-store experience and customer service provided by Best Buy employees.

title: Amazon’s not the only warehouse hiring in Fresno. Ulta Beauty looking for workers, too
summary: Ulta Beauty is opening a new 670,500-square-foot distribution center in Fresno, expected to employ about 540 workers, possibly up to 1,000 during peak seasons. This facility, Ulta's only one in California, will serve 400 stores and online orders across the western U.S. and is located near Amazon's new fulfillment warehouse, collectively bringing over 2,000 new jobs to the area. Ulta is actively hiring for various positions, from leadership roles to material handlers, with starting pay ranging from $13 to $18 per hour.

title: What you need to know about investing in global funds
summary: This article explains what global funds are, how they differ, and provides insights into investing in them. It features an interview with global fund manager Jake Robbins, who discusses his targeted approach to selecting companies. The article also lists several passive and active global funds, offering ideas for investors.

title: The RealReal’s Radical Vision of Secondhand Luxury
summary: The RealReal, an online luxury consignment store, offers an authentic experience for secondhand luxury goods, employing specialists to verify items like Hermès and Chanel handbags. Founded by Julie Wainwright in 2011, the company aims to make high fashion accessible while guaranteeing authenticity, differentiating itself from general e-commerce sites like Amazon. The RealReal provides a curated shopping experience both online and in its physical stores, offering educational workshops and professionally photographed items.

title: Target cuts delivery fee by almost half, putting pressure on Walmart, Amazon
summary: Target is slashing its next-day delivery fee for household staples by nearly half, from $4.99 to $2.99, as it rolls out its Restock service nationwide. This move aims to compete with Amazon and Walmart by leveraging Target's stores for faster fulfillment. Customers using a Target branded credit/debit card will receive free delivery through this service.

title: Presentation outlines vision for ‘Microchip 2.0’ - 16 May 2018 - Tempe Technologies
summary: Norbert Siedhoff, European sales director for Microchip Technology, presented the company's "Microchip 2.0" vision to the South African industry, emphasizing its evolution from a component manufacturer to a solution provider through strategic acquisitions and R&D. The presentation highlighted global mega trends influencing the company's modern strategy, with Microchip aiming to keep pace with rapid technological advancement. The event, hosted by Tempe Technologies, also previewed a shift from "Summer School" training to more focused quarterly events and included a demonstration of secure connectivity using Amazon Web Services.

title: George Soros' fund bought $35 million of Tesla bonds while loading up on Amazon, Netflix stock
summary: George Soros' investment firm, Soros Fund Management, purchased $35 million worth of Tesla convertible bonds in the first quarter of 2018, providing significant backing to the troubled electric carmaker. The fund also made substantial investments in Amazon and Netflix stock, acquiring 51,200 shares of Amazon and 148,500 shares of Netflix, while simultaneously divesting its holdings in Twitter. These moves offer insight into Soros Fund Management's investment strategy during a period of market volatility for some tech giants.

title: Stryker, J&J and Abbott ranked as top companies to work at in the U.S.
summary: Stryker, Johnson & Johnson, and Abbott have been recognized by LinkedIn as top U.S. companies to work for in 2018, based on data points from LinkedIn members. The article highlights reasons for their rankings, including company culture, comprehensive benefits, and responsiveness to employee needs, alongside employee testimonials from GlassDoor. These medical device giants also ranked highly on Medical Design & Outsourcing's Big 100 list based on revenue.

title: Amazon Prime members will get an additional 10% discount on Whole Foods items
summary: Amazon Prime members will receive an additional 10% discount on Whole Foods Market sale items, starting in Florida and expanding nationwide later in the summer. This discount applies to hundreds of products and weekly best-selling items. Customers can access the offer by scanning a Prime code at checkout or using their phone number.

title: Pending S.P. Richards Deal, Essendant Gets Buyout Offer From Staples
summary: Staples has made a buyout offer to Essendant, initiating a bidding war just five days after Essendant announced a merger with Genuine Parts Company's S.P. Richards. Essendant is currently weighing both proposals, with Staples making an all-cash offer potentially "significantly in excess" of $11.50 per share, while GPC enhanced its merger agreement with a contingent cash payment. This move by Staples, owned by Sycamore Partners, underscores its strategic shift towards expanding in the B2B supply market.

title: Hey Amazon, Kroger’s new delivery partner operates almost entirely on robots
summary: Kroger has announced a partnership with UK-based online grocery company Ocado, known for its highly automated warehouses utilizing AI-powered robots. This move allows Kroger to significantly expand its e-commerce capabilities in the U.S. and is seen as a direct challenge to Amazon's growing presence in the grocery market. The partnership involves Kroger licensing Ocado's technology and increasing its stake in the company, with plans for 20 new robot-operated warehouses in the U.S. over three years.

title: Kroger inks Ocado grocery delivery deal to battle Amazon threat
summary: U.S. supermarket giant Kroger Co has partnered with British online grocer Ocado to build robotically operated warehouses, aiming to boost its delivery business and compete with Amazon.com Inc. This exclusive deal, Ocado's first in the U.S., caused Ocado's shares to soar while Kroger's rose slightly, with investors reassured about future earnings. The partnership is seen as transformative for Kroger and a significant move in the evolving U.S. grocery market.

title: Hain Celestial’s ‘Natural’ Niche Has Gone Mainstream. Now What Does It Do?
summary: Hain Celestial, a pioneer in organic and natural products, is facing significant challenges despite previously thriving on consumer demand. Increased competition, changing consumer tastes, retailer consolidation, and the entry of Amazon into the grocery market are shrinking its margins and U.S. sales, making it a potential takeover target.

title: Academy Sports taps Foot Locker’s Ken Hicks as CEO
summary: Academy, Ltd., operating as Academy Sports + Outdoors, has appointed Ken Hicks as its new chairman and CEO. Hicks, formerly CEO of Foot Locker, is tasked with leading the company in a challenging retail landscape. He brings extensive experience from his prior role where he reversed negative same-store sales at Foot Locker.

title: Why did Flipkart and eBay India part ways?
summary: The article explains the reasons behind the parting of ways between Flipkart and eBay India following Walmart's acquisition of Flipkart. Key factors include eBay's underperforming India business, the opportunity to realize a quick profit from selling its holdings, intellectual property rights complexities regarding user agreements, and Walmart's strategy to avoid conflicts of interest and ease regulatory scrutiny from the Competition Commission of India. This split positions eBay to re-enter India as an independent entity, fostering competition.

title: Kroger Buys Home Chef for $200M as Meal Kits Continue March into Grocery Stores
summary: Kroger is acquiring meal kit company Home Chef for $200 million, a move that highlights the shift of meal kits from mail-order to in-store grocery items. Home Chef will operate as a Kroger subsidiary, maintaining its e-commerce business while also taking over Kroger's "meal solutions portfolio" and expanding its presence in Kroger's 2,800 stores. This acquisition allows Kroger to quickly scale its presence in the growing meal kit market, building on Home Chef's existing infrastructure and data, and is part of Kroger's broader strategy to enhance its technological relevance and delivery logistics.

title: U-Haul Self-Storage Investor Mark Schoen Named Richest Person in Arizo
summary: Mark V. Shoen, a significant shareholder in U-Haul International Inc.'s parent company AMERCO and owner of a large private self-storage operation, has been named the richest person in Arizona by "Forbes." While Forbes reported his net worth at $3 billion, the Bloomberg Billionaires Index estimated it at $5.58 billion, attributing his wealth to his substantial ownership in AMERCO and control of approximately 47 million square feet of storage space through various brands. This article highlights the discrepancy in reported net worths and details Shoen's extensive self-storage holdings.

title: Kroger buys Home Chef meal-kit delivery service
summary: Kroger announced its acquisition of Home Chef, the largest private meal-kit delivery service in the US, for $200 million. This strategic move aims to expand Kroger's meal-kit business and enhance its online and subscription capabilities to compete with other online food delivery services. Kroger could potentially pay an additional $500 million to Home Chef over the next five years based on sales milestones.

title: Kroger buys meal kit maker Home Chef for $200M
summary: Kroger has acquired meal kit company Home Chef for $200 million, with potential additional incentives up to $500 million if performance goals are met. Home Chef will continue its e-commerce operations while also offering its meal kits in Kroger stores and online, and will take over Kroger's existing meal solutions portfolio. This acquisition positions Kroger to compete more strongly in the evolving meal kit market, integrating valuable culinary expertise and customer data.

title: Michigan offered Amazon $4 billion package to build HQ2 in Detroit
summary: Michigan offered Amazon.com Inc. a $4 billion incentive package to build its second North American headquarters (HQ2) in Detroit, according to documents released by the Michigan Economic Development Corp. The offer, which included significant tax abatements and other incentives, highlights the intense competition among states for large investments. Despite the substantial offer, Detroit did not make Amazon's final selection, with reasons cited including public transit issues and talent attraction.

title: Spending Boom in China's Smaller Cities
summary: Consumption in China’s smaller cities is expected to triple between 2017 and 2030, driven by favorable government policies, population growth, higher household incomes, and increased willingness to spend. Morgan Stanley predicts these lower-tier cities will be the primary engine for China's overall private consumption market, with significant implications for consumer-focused industries and global investors. Key factors include a more flexible Hukou policy, improved infrastructure, and a stronger consumer appetite for discretionary spending due to lower housing costs.

title: Urban Outfitters launches third-party marketplace, tests self-checkout
summary: Urban Outfitters has launched an online marketplace for third-party sellers and is testing a self-checkout experience in one of its stores. The retailer is also investing in its digital infrastructure, including new iOS apps and accepting Apple Pay and Afterpay, following strong digital growth in Q1 2019. These moves aim to broaden product selection, enhance customer experience, and increase sales.

title: Anjali Sud was rejected from dozens of investment banks. Now she's the CEO of Vimeo
summary: Anjali Sud, CEO of Vimeo, faced numerous rejections from investment banks after graduating from Wharton. Despite initially struggling in a tough boarding school, she persevered, eventually taking an unconventional path through a small firm and Amazon before leading Vimeo. Sud's story highlights the value of diversity of experience, creating one's own opportunities, and not fearing failure.

title: How Amazon helped ex-Googler turn mom’s money into a billion dollars | Business News
summary: Steven Yang, an ex-Googler, leveraged his mother's money and Amazon's platform to build Anker Innovations, a consumer electronics company valued at over $1 billion. Anker, known for smartphone accessories and household products, has secured deals with Walmart and Best Buy, and Yang is considering an IPO for further expansion. The company's success highlights the potential of selling through Amazon while navigating fierce competition and the advantages of being embedded in Shenzhen's supply chain.

title: Netflix's Data-Driven Strategy Strengthens Claim For 'Best Original Content' In 2018
summary: Netflix's data-driven strategy has cemented its position as a leader in original content, with 39% of U.S. consumers rating its programming as best. The company's vertically integrated ecosystem allows it to use consumer data to guide content licensing and recommendations, a method exemplified by the success of "House of Cards." This approach distinguishes Netflix from competitors like Amazon, leading to significant market outperformance, including an all-time high stock price and a market cap exceeding Disney's in May 2018.

title: Microsoft is now more valuable than Alphabet — by about $10 billion
summary: Microsoft has surpassed Alphabet in market capitalization, becoming the world's third most valuable company. This shift occurred as Microsoft's market value reached $749 billion compared to Alphabet's $739 billion, largely driven by significant growth in Microsoft's cloud computing business. Microsoft's stock surged 40 percent over the past 12 months, greatly outpacing Alphabet's gains.

title: These tech companies have the most stressed-out workers
summary: A survey by workplace app Blind revealed that 70.73% of Credit Karma employees suffer from job burnout, making it the highest among tech companies surveyed. Other companies with over 50% burnout rates include Expedia, Oracle, and Lyft, while Netflix had the lowest at 38.89%. The article highlights the significant impact of burnout, with a separate survey indicating it's responsible for nearly half of staff turnover in the U.S.

title: Judge approves a $142-million settlement over the Wells Fargo accounts scandal, calling it 'rough justice'
summary: A U.S. District Judge has approved a $142-million class-action settlement for Wells Fargo customers affected by the unauthorized accounts scandal. The settlement aims to compensate account holders who had accounts created without their consent, with an average payout of $35 per customer. Despite objections and acknowledgments of its imperfections, the judge deemed it "rough justice" and a better alternative than prolonged litigation, while some consumers plan to appeal the decision.

title: Assurant adding 300 jobs to bulk up tech center in Gwinnett
summary: Assurant, a $6 billion-a-year insurance company, is adding 300 jobs to expand its technology arm in Gwinnett County, Georgia. This expansion involves a new tech support center in Duluth, catering to the growing demand for device insurance and support for smart devices. The company plans to recruit primarily from the local Gwinnett County and metro Atlanta talent pool for positions including technical support analysts, supervisors, and trainers.

title: Target launches same-day delivery in Milwaukee
summary: Target is expanding its same-day delivery service to Milwaukee and other select Wisconsin markets through its subsidiary Shipt. This service will be accessible to over 860,000 households in Wisconsin. The move follows similar expansions by other major retailers in the region.
